marking_schemes.question_text: Give the six-figure grid reference for the temple that is located to the south west of Pithapura settlement.
key_points: Six-figure grid reference 201215 or 202215 accepted
common_errors: Candidates placed third and sixth digits incorrectly, e.g. writing 205211 instead of 201215
Interchanging eastings and northings
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure students understand the concept of six-figure grid references. Third digit is the subdivided easting, sixth digit is the subdivided northing.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the four-figure grid reference for a settlement where people of the region meet socially and for trade at least once in a year.
common_errors: Candidates interchanged eastings and northings, e.g. writing 2216 instead of 1622
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Tell students that Eastings are to be written before Northings. Left side easting and lower side northing must be taken into consideration.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the pattern of drainage seen in the grid square 2118?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 2118 – Radial pattern.
key_points: Radial drainage pattern
marking_schemes.model_answer: Radial pattern
common_errors: Candidates wrote radical / centripetal / water flowing in all directions / trellised / dendritic instead of radial
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify drainage patterns to students and give sufficient practice to identify them. Emphasise correct spelling of all important terms.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the pattern of settlement seen in the grid square 1923?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1923 – Nucleated / Compact / Clustered. (Any one term)
key_points: Nucleated or Compact or Clustered (any one)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Nucleated / Compact / Clustered
common_errors: Candidates wrote nuclear / linear / houses are close instead of nucleated/compact/clustered
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain settlement patterns using diagrams and show students examples of various types on the toposheet.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: What do each of the two numbers (281 printed in black colour and 20 printed in red colour) in the grid square 1818 indicate?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 281 – Spot height/altitude of 281 m above mean sea level. 20 – Distance stone along the metalled road/milestone.
key_points: 281 indicates spot height / altitude of 281 m above mean sea level
20 indicates distance stone along the metalled road / milestone
marking_schemes.model_answer: The number 281 printed in black indicates the spot height, i.e. the altitude of that point is 281 metres above mean sea level. The number 20 printed in red indicates a distance stone/milestone along the metalled road.
common_errors: For 281, candidates wrote height / approximate height / longitude instead of spot height
For 20, candidates wrote kilometre stone instead of distance stone / milestone
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make students aware that the answer of what the numbers in a grid indicate is also given in the index below the map. Train students to read the index.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Name any two man-made features in grid square 2419.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Man-made features – Cart track / lined perennial well / permanent hut / unlined perennial well / cultivated land / footpath (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Cart track, lined perennial well, permanent hut, unlined perennial well, cultivated land, footpath
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two man-made features in grid square 2419 are cart track and lined perennial well (any two from: cart track, lined perennial well, permanent hut, unlined perennial well, cultivated land, footpath).
common_errors: Candidates wrote temple or tank which was not found in grid square 2419
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Be well equipped with the information on toposheet in order to guide students properly.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Name any two natural features in grid square 2118.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Natural features – Hill / seasonal stream / rocky slope / forest area / valley / spur (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Hill, seasonal stream, rocky slope, forest area, valley, spur
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two natural features in grid square 2118 are hill and seasonal stream (any two from: hill, seasonal stream, rocky slope, forest area, valley, spur).
common_errors: Candidates wrote trees/river instead of stream/contour line/ridge
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain concepts such as: trees are natural or grown by man; a river is broader than a stream; a contour line is made on map only and is not a feature; ridge is an elongated hill.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the significance of the fire line in grid square 2417?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Fire line is made to protect the forest from spread of forest fire.
key_points: Fire line is made to protect the forest from the spread of forest fire
marking_schemes.model_answer: A fire line is a cleared strip in the forest made to prevent the spread of forest fire from one part of the forest to another.
common_errors: Candidates wrote its meaning instead of its significance
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure students understand the difference between stating the meaning and the significance of a map feature.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the significance of the water body found in grid square 2221?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is a reservoir where river water is stored by constructing a dam / embankment. This water is used for irrigation through canal / for providing water for nearby areas.
key_points: It is a reservoir where river water is stored by constructing a dam/embankment
Used for irrigation through canal / providing water for nearby areas
marking_schemes.model_answer: The water body in grid square 2221 is a reservoir where river water is stored by constructing a dam or embankment. This water is used for irrigation through canals or for providing water supply to nearby areas.
common_errors: Majority of candidates did not write the significance; several wrote only the name of the feature such as tank/reservoir/water storage
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify to students the meaning of terms printed on the map to enable them to answer significance-based questions.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the area of the region between 16 and 19 Eastings and 18 and 22 Northings. Give your answer in kilometre square.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 12 km2
key_points: Area = 12 km²
Unit must be stated as km²
marking_schemes.model_answer: The area of the region between Eastings 16–19 and Northings 18–22 is 12 km².
common_errors: Some candidates did not write the unit km²
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay stress on expressing area with proper units. Advise students to show calculations as per the scale of the map and write the answer in the unit asked.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: The water in some of the wells in the north west quarter of the map is not fit for drinking.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The water in some of the wells is brackish/salty/saline.
key_points: The water in some wells is brackish / salty / saline
marking_schemes.model_answer: The water in some of the wells in the north west quarter is not fit for drinking because it is brackish/salty/saline.
common_errors: Candidates wrote that the water was not fit as it was dirty / polluted / contaminated / filled with sand or silt
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to make use of the terms which are printed on the map (saline wells are marked on the toposheet).
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: The region near Anadra and Gulabganj has many causeways.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: There are many streams / seasonal streams in the region and causeways have to be built when metalled roads are constructed to enable it to cross the stream.
key_points: There are many streams/seasonal streams in the region
Causeways are built when metalled roads are constructed to cross streams
marking_schemes.model_answer: The region near Anadra and Gulabganj has many causeways because there are numerous seasonal streams in the area, and causeways are constructed along metalled roads to allow them to cross these streams.
common_errors: Most candidates wrote that people had to travel so there were causeways
Some wrote the meaning of causeway
A few wrote that a causeway was a bridge
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain the difference between a causeway and a bridge.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the main means of irrigation used by people living in the area shown on the map?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: lined perennial well/lined well
key_points: Lined perennial well / lined well
marking_schemes.model_answer: Lined perennial well / lined well
common_errors: Some candidates wrote tube well instead of lined perennial well
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students in using correct terms for conventional symbols on the toposheet. Insist on the term 'lined perennial well' rather than just 'well'.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the main occupation of the people of the region shown on the map?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cultivation/agriculture/farming.
key_points: Cultivation / agriculture / farming
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cultivation / agriculture / farming
common_errors: Some candidates wrote animal rearing and forestry, having overlooked the word 'main' occupation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach land use pattern by using colours as the main clue for identifying the same.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Which according to you is the most important settlement? Give a reason to support your answer.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Anadra - it has a metalled road passing near it / Dispensary / Dak-Bungalow / Post and Telegraph office / Police Chowki.
key_points: Anadra is the most important settlement
Reason: it has a metalled road / Dispensary / Dak-Bungalow / Post and Telegraph office / Police Chowki (any valid reason)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Anadra is the most important settlement because it has a metalled road passing near it and is served by civic amenities such as a Dispensary, Dak-Bungalow, Post and Telegraph office, and Police Chowki.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the type of settlement pattern instead of naming a specific settlement
Some candidates were unable to provide a reason to support their selection
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice to students in answering questions on important settlement, comparison of settlement, and general pattern.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Name any two means of transport used by the people living in the area shown on the map extract.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Metalled road / Cart track / Pack track / Foot path. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Metalled road, Cart track, Pack track, Foot path
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two means of transport used by people in the area are cart track and metalled road (any two from: metalled road, cart track, pack track, footpath).
common_errors: Candidates wrote mode of transport (carts, car, automobile) instead of means of transport
A few candidates wrote general answers like roadways and railways which are not accepted
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the difference between means of transport and mode of transport. Tell students that general answers such as roadways and railways are not accepted in toposheet questions.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label the Gangetic Plain.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Gangetic Plain shaded and labelled in the correct region of North India.
key_points: Gangetic Plain correctly shaded within its boundaries
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade the Gangetic Plain in the northern plains region of India (not extending into Nepal or Bangladesh) and label it.
common_errors: Shading went up to Nepal and Bangladesh beyond correct boundary
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure marking in the maps of all places mentioned in syllabus is practised regularly. Advise students to consult an atlas.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label an area of laterite soil in North India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — area of laterite soil in North India correctly shaded and labelled.
key_points: Laterite soil area in North India correctly located and shaded
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade an area of laterite soil in North India (not anywhere in India) and label it as Laterite Soil.
common_errors: Some candidates marked the area anywhere in India
Shading was too vast in a few answer scripts
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the areas where each type of soil is found by using a map so students are able to correlate.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the Karakoram Mountains.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Karakoram Mountains correctly marked and labelled in the northern region.
key_points: Karakoram Mountains correctly marked as a range (not a peak)
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark the Karakoram Mountains in the northernmost part of India/Jammu & Kashmir using the correct symbol for a mountain range and label it.
common_errors: A few candidates marked the range using a triangle symbol, which is used for a peak not a range
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure students understand that a triangle is used for a peak and not for a range.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and name the Palk Strait.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Palk Strait correctly marked between India and Sri Lanka and labelled.
key_points: Palk Strait correctly marked between India and Sri Lanka (not extended into Gulf of Mannar)
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark the Palk Strait between the south-eastern tip of India and Sri Lanka using a dotted line or arrowhead and label it as Palk Strait.
common_errors: Many candidates extended it into the Gulf of Mannar
Some shaded the region instead of marking with an arrow
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students to mark a strait by using a dotted line or an arrow.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label the river Cauveri.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — River Cauvery correctly shaded from head to mouth and labelled.
key_points: River Cauvery correctly shaded from source to mouth
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade the river Cauvery from its source in the Western Ghats (Karnataka) to its mouth in the Bay of Bengal (Tamil Nadu) and label it.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to shade all rivers from their head to the mouth.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and name Mumbai.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Mumbai correctly marked on the west coast and labelled.
key_points: Mumbai correctly marked on the west coast of India
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark Mumbai on the west coast of India (Maharashtra) with a dot on the land portion and label it.
common_errors: Some candidates made a bigger dot than required
Some candidates shaded it into the sea
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise that port cities must be marked on the land portion and must not extend into the sea.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and name the Nathu La Pass.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Nathu La Pass correctly marked in Sikkim region and labelled.
key_points: Nathu La Pass correctly marked in Sikkim/northeastern border region
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark the Nathu La Pass on the border of Sikkim and China using the correct pass symbol and label it.
common_errors: Most candidates were unable to mark it correctly
Several candidates marked it as horizontal lines (=) which was incorrect
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that marking of all places mentioned in the syllabus is practised regularly by students.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and name Digboi.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Digboi correctly marked in Assam and labelled.
key_points: Digboi correctly marked in Assam (north-east India)
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark Digboi in the state of Assam in north-east India and label it.
common_errors: Most candidates were unable to mark Digboi correctly
Several marked it more to the north
Many marked it closer to the river
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that marking of all places in the syllabus is practised regularly. Advise students to consult an atlas.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and name the Deccan Plateau.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Deccan Plateau correctly shaded and labelled.
key_points: Deccan Plateau correctly shaded within its boundaries
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade the Deccan Plateau in the peninsular region of India, bounded by the Satpura range in the north and the Eastern and Western Ghats on either side, and label it.
common_errors: Deccan Plateau shading went much beyond its boundary on the northern side
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to mark Satpura, Nilgiri, Eastern and Western Ghats very lightly and then shade the Deccan Plateau between them. Train students to mark Deccan as a whole or as dissected.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label the river Jhelum.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — River Jhelum correctly shaded and labelled.
key_points: River Jhelum correctly shaded from source to the point it joins the Indus
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade the river Jhelum from its source in Kashmir to the point where it joins the river Indus/Chenab, and label it.
common_errors: Some candidates got confused between tributaries of river Indus and marked Jhelum incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to shade all rivers from their head to the mouth and tributaries from their head to the point where they join the main river.

marking_schemes.question_text: What type of wind is 'Monsoon'? What is its direction during summer?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Periodic wind; direction during summer is south west
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is a periodic wind. Its direction during summer is southwest.
key_points: Monsoon is a periodic wind
Its direction during summer is south west
marking_schemes.model_answer: Monsoon is a periodic wind. Its direction during summer is south west.
common_errors: Many candidates wrote vague answers or the meaning of the term monsoon instead of the type of wind
Some wrote sea to land instead of south west direction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain thoroughly about the monsoon, its mechanism, types, origin and direction. Make a clear comparison between monsoon winds and land and sea breeze.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two characteristics of the Indian monsoon.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Erratic in nature / Unevenly distributed / mostly orographic type / occurs mainly in four months.
key_points: Erratic in nature / unevenly distributed
Mostly orographic type / occurs mainly in four months
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two characteristics of the Indian monsoon are: (1) it is erratic and unevenly distributed across regions, and (2) it occurs mainly over four months and is predominantly orographic in nature.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote factors affecting monsoon instead of characteristics of the Indian monsoon
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain to students the difference between factors affecting monsoons and characteristics of monsoons.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the summer season in India, mention the duration of the summer season in India.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: March, April, May / March to May
marking_schemes.scheme_text: March, April, May / March to May
key_points: March to May (March, April, May)
marking_schemes.model_answer: March to May
common_errors: Some candidates included the S.W. Monsoon season and wrote March to September as the duration of summers
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make students understand the seasons in India and ensure they learn their duration.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to the summer season in India, what is the atmospheric pressure condition during summer season over the central part of India?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: In central part of India there is low pressure.
key_points: Low pressure prevails in the central part of India during summer
marking_schemes.model_answer: Low pressure
common_errors: Several candidates wrote high pressure instead of low pressure
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay stress on reasoning-based questions in practice tests to ensure better understanding.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Goa receives heavier rainfall than Puducherry.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Goa is located on the windward side of western ghats so Arabian Sea Branch of south west monsoon bring heavier rainfall and Puducherry is located on the eastern coast and receives lighter rainfall from North East Monsoon.
key_points: Goa is on the windward side of the Western Ghats and receives heavy rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch of the South West Monsoon
Puducherry is on the eastern coast and receives lighter rainfall from the North East Monsoon
marking_schemes.model_answer: Goa is located on the windward side of the Western Ghats, and the Arabian Sea branch of the South West Monsoon brings heavy orographic rainfall to it. Puducherry, located on the eastern coast, receives lighter rainfall mainly from the North East Monsoon.
common_errors: Many candidates explained either about Goa or Puducherry but not both
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to explain about both the cities in their answers in questions where two cities are mentioned.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Mawsynram receives the highest average annual rainfall.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Mawsynram experiences Orographic rainfall as it is located on windward side of Garo hill. Bay of Bengal branch of South West Monsoon brings heavy rain to this area / funnel shape of Garo, Khasi, Jaintia hill lead to trapping of clouds leading to more rains.
key_points: Mawsynram is located on the windward side of the Garo-Khasi hills
Bay of Bengal branch of South West Monsoon causes orographic/heavy rainfall
Funnel shape of Garo, Khasi, Jaintia hills traps clouds leading to more rain
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mawsynram receives the highest rainfall because it is located on the windward side of the Garo-Khasi-Jaintia hills. The Bay of Bengal branch of the South West Monsoon is funnelled and trapped by the funnel-shaped arrangement of hills, causing extremely heavy orographic rainfall.
common_errors: Some candidates did not write key words such as windward side / Garo-Khasi hills / clouds trapped due to position of hills
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make use of maps, smart boards, and diagrams to ensure concept building.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Mangaluru is cooler than Delhi in summer season.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Mangalore has a coastal location, but Delhi lies in the interior. Due to distance from the sea, Mangalore is cooler than Delhi in summer.
key_points: Mangaluru has a coastal location; Delhi lies in the interior
Coastal location moderates temperature; interior location leads to extreme heat in summer
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mangaluru is cooler than Delhi in summer because it has a coastal location where the sea moderates temperatures, while Delhi lies in the interior of the country far from the moderating influence of the sea, leading to extreme heat in summer.
common_errors: Some candidates gave difference in altitude as the reason instead of coastal vs interior location
A few candidates wrote only about one city
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to explain about both the cities in their answers in questions where two cities are mentioned.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the data of distribution of temperature and rain for station X (Jan:10°C/2cm, Feb:11°C/1cm, Mar:23°C/0cm, Apr:35°C/5cm, May:39°C/15cm, Jun:42°C/62cm, Jul:40°C/71cm, Aug:33°C/81cm, Sep:30°C/59cm, Oct:25°C/12cm, Nov:13°C/10cm, Dec:11°C/3cm). Is Station X in the coastal area or in the interior of the country?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is in the interior.
key_points: Station X is in the interior of the country
marking_schemes.model_answer: Interior
common_errors: Some candidates wrote coastal instead of interior
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give sufficient practice to students in answering questions based on climatic data.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the data of distribution of temperature and rain for station X (Jan:10°C/2cm, Feb:11°C/1cm, Mar:23°C/0cm, Apr:35°C/5cm, May:39°C/15cm, Jun:42°C/62cm, Jul:40°C/71cm, Aug:33°C/81cm, Sep:30°C/59cm, Oct:25°C/12cm, Nov:13°C/10cm, Dec:11°C/3cm). Calculate the total annual rainfall for Station X.
key_points: Total annual rainfall = 321 cm
Unit must be stated as cm
marking_schemes.model_answer: 321 cm
common_errors: Some candidates did not write the unit in their answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay stress that in questions related to calculations, it is important to write the unit.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the data of distribution of temperature and rain for station X (Jan:10°C/2cm, Feb:11°C/1cm, Mar:23°C/0cm, Apr:35°C/5cm, May:39°C/15cm, Jun:42°C/62cm, Jul:40°C/71cm, Aug:33°C/81cm, Sep:30°C/59cm, Oct:25°C/12cm, Nov:13°C/10cm, Dec:11°C/3cm). Name the wind that brings most of the rainfall to Station X.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: South West Monsoon
key_points: South West Monsoon
marking_schemes.model_answer: South West Monsoon
common_errors: Some candidates gave N.E. Monsoon or western disturbance as the answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the monsoon mechanism and its direction thoroughly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the Indian soil which is formed due to the weathering of basic igneous rocks.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Black soil / Regur / Black cotton soil
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Black soil/ Regur/Black cotton soil
key_points: Black soil / Regur / Black cotton soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: Black soil / Regur / Black cotton soil
common_errors: Many candidates associated basic igneous rock with red soil
Several wrote all in-situ soils: red, laterite and black
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Revise the topic on rocks (acid igneous, basic igneous and metamorphic rocks) thoroughly and train students to answer such questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name two states of India where black soil (formed due to weathering of basic igneous rocks) is found.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Any two of: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, parts of Tamil Nadu
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Maharashtra / Gujarat / Madhya Pradesh / Andhra Pradesh / Karnataka / parts of Tamil Nadu (Any two)
key_points: Any two states from: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, parts of Tamil Nadu
marking_schemes.model_answer: Maharashtra and Gujarat (any two from: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, parts of Tamil Nadu).
common_errors: A large number of candidates were unable to answer this as it was interlinked with part (i)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the areas where each type of soil is found by using a map so students are able to correlate.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name an important transported soil of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Alluvial soil
key_points: Alluvial soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: Alluvial soil
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain to the students the transported or ex-situ soils with examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the soil that is rich in iron oxide.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Red soil / Laterite soil (Any one)
key_points: Red soil or Laterite soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: Red soil / Laterite soil
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the properties/characteristics of each type of soils found in India as per the scope of the syllabus.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Terrace farming is an ideal soil conservation method for hilly regions.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Terraces check the speed of running water and thus reduce the chance for erosion.
key_points: Terraces check the speed of running water and thus reduce the chance of soil erosion
marking_schemes.model_answer: Terrace farming is ideal for hilly regions because the step-like terraces check the speed of running water flowing down the slopes, thereby reducing the chance of soil erosion.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote lengthy explanations with key words missing
Some related it to wind erosion
A few wrote the meaning of terrace farming instead of explaining its relevance for hilly areas
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain clearly the different agents of erosion (wind and running water) and conservation methods used for them.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Dry farming is preferred in areas with red soil.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Red soil is ideal for dry farming because it is porous and does not retain moisture.
key_points: Red soil is porous and does not retain moisture, making it suitable for dry farming
marking_schemes.model_answer: Dry farming is preferred in areas with red soil because red soil is porous and does not retain moisture, making it unsuitable for crops requiring constant irrigation and thus ideal for dry farming techniques.
common_errors: Several candidates wrote the meaning of dry farming instead of explaining the characteristics of red soil
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the properties/characteristics of each type of soil and relate to farming methods.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Wind is a common agent of soil erosion in arid regions.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Soil erosion by wind is common in arid regions because arid areas do not support vegetation and since there are no roots to hold the soil together, the wind can carry away the loose soil easily/wind speed is high due to absence of obstruction.
key_points: Arid areas do not support vegetation so there are no roots to hold the soil
Wind carries away the loose soil easily / wind speed is high due to absence of obstructions
marking_schemes.model_answer: Wind is a common agent of soil erosion in arid regions because these areas lack vegetation and there are no plant roots to bind the soil together. The absence of obstructions also results in high wind speeds, which easily carry away the loose topsoil.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain clearly the different agents of erosion (wind and running water) and their associated conservation methods.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly answer the following: Mention one way in which man is responsible for soil erosion.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Man is responsible for soil erosion because of large scale deforestation done for agriculture / industrialisation / urbanisation / he allows his livestock to overgraze land / faulty farming practices / mining / construction / quarrying / excessive usage of chemical fertiliser, pesticide or insecticide / shifting agriculture. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: large scale deforestation, overgrazing, faulty farming practices, mining/construction/quarrying, excessive use of chemical fertilisers/pesticides, shifting agriculture
marking_schemes.model_answer: Man is responsible for soil erosion through large-scale deforestation for agriculture, industrialisation or urbanisation, which removes the vegetative cover that binds the soil.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach all agents of soil erosion including man along with his role. Discuss methods adopted to check the impact.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly answer the following: How can deepening of the river bed help in preventing soil erosion?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Deepening the river bed increases the capacity of the river to hold water which then will not overflow to cause soil erosion.
key_points: Deepening the river bed increases the river's capacity to hold water
This prevents overflow which would otherwise cause soil erosion on the banks
marking_schemes.model_answer: Deepening the river bed increases the capacity of the river to hold water, so the river does not overflow its banks and cause soil erosion in surrounding areas.
common_errors: Some candidates could not comprehend the meaning of deepening of the river bed and its association with soil erosion
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the advantages of desilting and how it helps in controlling floods and in turn reduces soil erosion.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly answer the following: Mention a physical characteristic of Laterite soil.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Red in colour / dry / porous / hardens when dry / coarse / does not retain moisture / soft and friable / colour varies from red to brown to yellow (any one)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is red in colour / dry / porous / hardens when dry / coarse / does not retain moisture / soft and friable / colour varies from red to brown to yellow. (Any one)
key_points: Any one physical characteristic: red in colour / dry / porous / hardens when dry / coarse / does not retain moisture / soft and friable / colour varies from red to brown to yellow
marking_schemes.model_answer: Laterite soil is red in colour / porous / hardens when dry / does not retain moisture (any one physical characteristic).
accepted_alternatives: Colour varies from red to brown to yellow
common_errors: Some candidates wrote its chemical composition and acidic nature which is a chemical, not a physical, characteristic
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify to students that physical characteristics relate to colour, texture and moisture retentivity of soil while chemical characteristics relate to the chemical composition of soil.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two reasons to explain as to why we need to conserve our forest resource.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Forests must be conserved because they have a favourable effect on the climate or temperature and rain / help in soil conservation / flood control measure / maintains the ecological balance / habitat of wild life / provide forest products / places of tourist interest / become a source of humus / check extension of sand dune / prevent global warming / recharge ground water. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: favourable effect on climate/temperature and rainfall, soil conservation, flood control, ecological balance, habitat of wildlife, forest products, tourist interest, source of humus, check sand dune extension, prevent global warming, recharge ground water
marking_schemes.model_answer: We need to conserve forests because they help maintain ecological balance and regulate climate by influencing temperature and rainfall. They also provide habitat for wildlife, help in soil conservation, control floods, and prevent global warming.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Before starting the topic on natural vegetation, discuss at length the importance of forest as a resource.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two conditions required for the growth of Littoral Forest.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Temperature 26°C to 29°C / Rainfall – more than 200 cm / coastal climate / areas of tidal influence / salty water area.
key_points: Any two of: temperature 26°C to 29°C, rainfall more than 200 cm, coastal climate, areas of tidal influence, salty/brackish water area
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two conditions required for the growth of Littoral (Mangrove) forests are: temperature between 26°C and 29°C and rainfall of more than 200 cm in coastal areas under tidal influence.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote characteristics of the forest instead of conditions required for growth
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain in a tabular form the difference between conditions for growth of all types of natural vegetation belts and their characteristics.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one characteristic feature of the forest found in the Nilgiri Hills.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Vegetation consists of mixed deciduous and coniferous forests. The vegetation varies according to altitude. Consists of tropical montane forest - has deciduous, evergreen and alpine vegetation. (Any one point)
key_points: Any one of: mixed deciduous and coniferous forests, vegetation varies according to altitude, consists of tropical montane forest with deciduous/evergreen/alpine vegetation
marking_schemes.model_answer: The forests of the Nilgiri Hills consist of tropical montane (mountain) forests where the vegetation varies according to altitude, with a mix of deciduous, evergreen and coniferous species.
accepted_alternatives: Has deciduous, evergreen and alpine vegetation
common_errors: Some candidates could not identify/recall the vegetation type found in the Nilgiri Hills
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to learn the names of the trees found in each vegetation belt of India.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two reasons to explain as to why the Tropical Evergreen Forests are difficult to exploit for commercial purpose.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Thick undergrowth / inaccessible / Trees are not in pure stand / mixed stand / Heavy rainfall / Lack of transportation / Hard wood difficult to cut / Dark and dense / marshy area / very tall trees / water logging. (Any two points)
key_points: Any two of: thick undergrowth/inaccessible, trees not in pure stand/mixed stand, heavy rainfall, lack of transportation, hardwood difficult to cut, dark and dense/marshy/water logging
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical Evergreen Forests are difficult to exploit commercially because they have thick undergrowth making them inaccessible, and the trees grow in mixed stands (not pure stands), making selective logging difficult. Heavy rainfall and lack of transportation infrastructure further add to the challenges.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Develop the reasoning skills of students to enable them to answer application-based questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name any two trees found in Tropical Evergreen forests.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Any two of: Rosewood, Ironwood, Ebony, Cinchona, Mahogany, Bamboo
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Rosewood, Ironwood, Ebony, Cinchona, Mahogany, bamboo. (Any one)
key_points: Any two of: Rosewood, Ironwood, Ebony, Cinchona, Mahogany, Bamboo
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rosewood and Ebony (any two from: Rosewood, Ironwood, Ebony, Cinchona, Mahogany, Bamboo).
common_errors: Some candidates wrote names of tropical deciduous trees instead of evergreen trees
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to learn the names of the trees found in each vegetation belt of India.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly explain the following: The trees in the Tropical Desert Forest have stunted growth.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: This is due to non-availability of enough water for growth of trees.
key_points: Due to non-availability of enough water for the growth of trees
marking_schemes.model_answer: The trees in the Tropical Desert Forest have stunted growth due to the non-availability of sufficient water needed for healthy tree growth.
common_errors: Many candidates were unable to relate stunted growth to scarcity of water
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Develop the reasoning skills of students to enable them to answer application-based questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly explain the following: There is a gradual increase in the forest cover in India in recent times.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: This is due to check on deforestation / banning shifting agriculture / government initiative such as agroforestry, farm forestry, social forestry, Van Mahotsav, afforestation and re-afforestation.
key_points: Check on deforestation / banning shifting agriculture / government initiatives such as agroforestry, farm forestry, social forestry, Van Mahotsav, afforestation and re-afforestation
marking_schemes.model_answer: The gradual increase in forest cover in India is due to government initiatives such as agroforestry, social forestry, Van Mahotsav, afforestation and re-afforestation programmes, as well as checks on deforestation and banning of shifting agriculture.
common_errors: Several candidates wrote about the need to increase the forest cover instead of the methods adopted for forest conservation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Reinforce learning by frequently questioning students in different ways on the concepts taught.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly explain the following: The trees in Monsoon Deciduous forests shed their leaves for about 6-8 weeks during March and April.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Lack of sufficient moisture for leaves to withstand dry weather conditions / to conserve moisture / to reduce loss of water through transpiration / to have less surface area / subsoil water is not enough for trees to retain leaf cover / to survive heat and drought condition during autumn, spring and early summer.
key_points: Lack of sufficient moisture during dry season / to conserve moisture / to reduce loss of water through transpiration / to survive heat and drought conditions
marking_schemes.model_answer: Trees in Monsoon Deciduous forests shed their leaves during March and April because there is insufficient moisture during the dry season. Shedding leaves reduces water loss through transpiration, helping the trees conserve moisture and survive heat and drought conditions.
accepted_alternatives: To reduce loss of water through transpiration
Subsoil water not enough for trees to retain leaf cover
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the characteristics of the forest belt instead of giving reasons for leaf shedding
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give written assignments to students for them to gain confidence.

marking_schemes.question_text: 'The modern means of irrigation are gaining popularity.' Give two reasons to justify this statement.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: No loss of water due to evaporation and leakage / Use water economically / No wastage of water / help to conserve water / Do not cause soil erosion / Suitable for areas of low rain, high efficiency. (Any two points)
key_points: Any two of: no loss of water due to evaporation/leakage, use water economically/no wastage, do not cause soil erosion, suitable for areas of low rainfall/high efficiency
marking_schemes.model_answer: Modern means of irrigation are gaining popularity because they prevent water loss due to evaporation and leakage, ensuring economical use of water. They also do not cause soil erosion and are highly efficient, making them suitable for areas of low rainfall.
accepted_alternatives: High efficiency/suitable for low rainfall areas
common_errors: Many candidates wrote about traditional methods or the need for irrigation instead of advantages of modern means
Some candidates incorrectly stated that modern means were becoming popular because they were cheaper
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain to students the difference between traditional and modern means of irrigation along with the advantages and disadvantages of both categories.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two factors that favour the development of tube well irrigation in Punjab.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Ground water level is high / high water table / Soft nature of rocks which makes digging tube wells easy / soft soil / Availability of cheap HEP / fertile agricultural area / Productive area to compensate cost of tube well construction. (Any two points)
key_points: Any two of: high ground water level/high water table, soft nature of rocks/soft soil makes digging easy, availability of cheap HEP, fertile agricultural area/productive area to compensate cost
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two factors favouring tube well irrigation in Punjab are: (1) the ground water level/water table is high, making it easy to draw water, and (2) the soft nature of the soil and rocks makes digging tube wells relatively easy and economical.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote conditions necessary for tube-well development in general instead of factors specific to Punjab
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain advantages of any means of irrigation with reference to the particular area/state, related to the physiological and hydrological conditions of the area.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Most of the South Indian states are not suitable for development of canal irrigation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: South Indian states have uneven terrain hence they are not suitable for constructing canals / rivers are seasonal / hard rocks make it difficult to construct canals. (Any one point)
key_points: Any one of: uneven terrain not suitable for canal construction, rivers are seasonal, hard rocks make canal construction difficult
marking_schemes.model_answer: Most South Indian states are not suitable for canal irrigation because the terrain is uneven and undulating, making canal construction difficult. The rivers are also seasonal in nature, and the hard rocky terrain makes it difficult to dig canals.
accepted_alternatives: Hard rocks make it difficult to construct canals
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the answer in relation to inland transport
Some wrote about factors necessary for canal irrigation instead of why South India is not suitable
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the type of terrain necessary for the development of various means of irrigation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: There is an urgent need for water conservation in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: To meet the increasing demand of growing population / To provide water for irrigation and industrial use / increase crop production / To reduce the water scarcity / pollution of water / depleting ground water / wastage of water / rain is seasonal and unreliable. (Any one point)
key_points: Any one of: increasing demand of growing population, water for irrigation/industrial use, reduce water scarcity/pollution, depleting ground water, wastage of water, rain is seasonal and unreliable
marking_schemes.model_answer: There is an urgent need for water conservation in India to meet the increasing demand of the growing population, and because rainfall is seasonal and unreliable while ground water is rapidly depleting due to over-exploitation.
accepted_alternatives: To provide water for irrigation and industrial use
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the water crisis faced by India today and the reasons thereof along with the remedies for combatting water shortage.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Development of irrigation is essential for the growth of the agriculture sector of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Rainfall in India is seasonal / uncertain / unevenly distributed / annual crops need water all through the year / to maximize the agricultural production / To attain self sufficiency / Certain crops need more water / For success of green revolution. (Any one point)
key_points: Any one of: rainfall is seasonal/uncertain/unevenly distributed, annual crops need water throughout the year, to maximise agricultural production, to attain self-sufficiency, certain crops need more water, for success of green revolution
marking_schemes.model_answer: Development of irrigation is essential for the growth of agriculture because rainfall in India is seasonal, uncertain and unevenly distributed, while crops need water throughout the year to maximise production and attain self-sufficiency.
accepted_alternatives: Annual crops need water all through the year
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Relate the chapter on irrigation with the chapter on climate and explain the need for irrigation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly explain the following term: Inundation canal.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The canals that are taken out from the rivers without any regulating system like weirs, etc at their head / the canal that are filled with water only during floods.
key_points: Canals taken out from rivers without any regulating system like weirs at their head
Filled with water only during floods
marking_schemes.model_answer: An inundation canal is a canal taken out from a river without any regulating structure such as a weir at its head. It is filled with water only during the flood season when the river level is high.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain the two types of canals, their need along with the advantages and disadvantages of both types.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly explain the following term: Rooftop rainwater harvesting.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Rainwater can be collected over rooftop and collected water channelized through small PVC pipes into the underground pits, wells, etc.
key_points: Rainwater collected over the rooftop
Water channelized through small PVC pipes into underground pits, wells, etc.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rooftop rainwater harvesting is a method where rainwater falling on the rooftop is collected and channelized through small PVC pipes into underground pits or wells for storage and later use.
common_errors: Some candidates gave general answers such as 'rain water is collected' without specifying the rooftop mechanism
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students the difference between rainwater harvesting and rooftop rainwater harvesting.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly explain the following term: Surface water.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Water found on the surface of the earth in the form of rivers, lakes, ponds, etc. is called surface water.
key_points: Water found on the surface of the earth
In the form of rivers, lakes, ponds, etc.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Surface water is the water found on the surface of the earth in the form of rivers, lakes, ponds, and other water bodies.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote that surface water is the water found on the surface of the earth without giving any examples
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify to students the meaning of ground water or surface water with examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two advantages of using bio-gas as a source of power.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bio-gas is clean / non-polluting / cheap / the sludge left behind act as a rich fertilizer / can be installed with less capital investment / cost effective / eco-friendly / easily available / reduce dependence on fossil fuel / renewable / sustainable. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: clean/non-polluting, cheap/cost effective, sludge acts as rich fertilizer, less capital investment, eco-friendly, easily available, reduces dependence on fossil fuel, renewable/sustainable
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two advantages of using bio-gas are: (1) it is clean and non-polluting, making it eco-friendly, and (2) the sludge left behind after bio-gas generation acts as a rich organic fertilizer for agriculture.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the advantages and disadvantages of conventional sources of power and ensure students learn them by conducting regular tests.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name a metallic mineral for which the Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh is famous.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Manganese or Copper or Bauxite
key_points: Manganese or Copper or Bauxite
marking_schemes.model_answer: Manganese / Copper / Bauxite
common_errors: Some candidates wrote iron ore or magnesium instead of manganese
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the mining areas and uses of minerals in a tabular form to make learning and revision easier for students.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the multi-purpose project based on the River Sutlej.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: The Bhakra Nangal Dam / Bhakra Nangal project
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The Bhakra Nangal Dam/ Bhakra Nangal project
key_points: Bhakra Nangal Dam / Bhakra Nangal project
marking_schemes.model_answer: Bhakra Nangal Dam / Bhakra Nangal project
common_errors: Some candidates wrote only Bhakra Dam without the complete name
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instruct students to write the complete name of multipurpose projects.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Odisha has benefitted greatly from the Hirakud project.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The Hirakud project generates power / provides water for irrigation for both the kharif and rabi crops / controls floods on the River Mahanadi / soil conservation / fish culture / industrial growth / water supply / inland waterways. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: generates power, provides water for irrigation for kharif and rabi crops, controls floods on River Mahanadi, soil conservation, fish culture, industrial growth, water supply, inland waterways
marking_schemes.model_answer: Odisha has benefitted greatly from the Hirakud project because it generates hydroelectric power, provides water for irrigation for both kharif and rabi crops, and controls floods on the River Mahanadi.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Conduct oral and written tests regularly to ensure that students have learnt the facts.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Copper is used to make electric wires.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Copper is a good conductor of electricity / is ductile and malleable and so is used to make electric wires. (Any one)
key_points: Copper is a good conductor of electricity
Copper is ductile and malleable (any one)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Copper is used to make electric wires because it is a very good conductor of electricity and is also ductile and malleable, allowing it to be drawn into thin wires easily.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the mining areas and uses of minerals in a tabular form.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: India's location is advantageous for the generation of solar power.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: India lies between 8°N and 37°N with the Tropic of Cancer running through it and so receives a lot of sunlight with 300 clear days in a year. This is advantageous for the generation of solar power.
key_points: India lies between 8°N and 37°N with the Tropic of Cancer running through it
Receives a lot of sunlight / approximately 300 clear sunny days in a year
marking_schemes.model_answer: India's location between 8°N and 37°N, with the Tropic of Cancer passing through it, means it receives abundant sunlight with approximately 300 clear days per year, which is highly advantageous for the generation of solar power.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Conduct oral and written tests regularly to ensure students have learnt the facts.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly answer the following: Name a mineral used to generate nuclear power.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Uranium / Thorium / Beryllium/Plutonium/Zirconium (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Uranium, Thorium, Beryllium, Plutonium, Zirconium
marking_schemes.model_answer: Uranium / Thorium / Beryllium / Plutonium / Zirconium (any one)
common_errors: Some candidates named coal/petroleum/natural gas as minerals used to generate nuclear power
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the advantages and disadvantages of conventional and non-conventional sources of power.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly answer the following: Why is petroleum often referred to as 'liquid gold'?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Petroleum is a versatile mineral. It generates power / used as a fuel for vehicles and in factories / used as a raw material for products like plastics, tarpaulin, wax etc. / by-products like kerosene are very useful / Not even the smallest part of the crude oil goes waste or remains unused and is therefore called liquid gold / because of high economic value.
key_points: Petroleum is versatile: generates power, fuel for vehicles/factories, raw material for plastics/tarpaulin/wax, by-products like kerosene are useful
Not even the smallest part of crude oil goes to waste / high economic value
marking_schemes.model_answer: Petroleum is referred to as liquid gold because it is a highly versatile mineral — it generates power, is used as fuel for vehicles and factories, and serves as raw material for products like plastics, wax and tarpaulin. Not even the smallest part of crude oil goes unused, making it of extremely high economic value.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote about the colour of petrol as yellow, relating it to gold, instead of explaining its high economic value
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the reason to consider petroleum as liquid gold.

marking_schemes.question_text: Briefly answer the following: State one disadvantage of using coal as a source of power.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It leads to pollution / it is exhaustible / it is non-renewable / heavy transport cost / problem of disposal of residue / health hazard.
key_points: Any one of: leads to pollution, exhaustible/non-renewable, heavy transport cost, problem of disposal of residue, health hazard
marking_schemes.model_answer: One disadvantage of using coal as a source of power is that burning coal leads to air pollution, releasing harmful gases and particulates that pose health hazards. Coal is also a non-renewable and exhaustible resource.
common_errors: Many candidates wrote the calorific value of coal instead of its disadvantage as a source of power
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the advantages and disadvantages of conventional sources of power.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two steps taken by the government to boost agricultural production in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Promoting availability of good seeds to the farmers (high yielding variety) / Setting up of agriculture price commission to give better price for agricultural products / Providing easy loans to the farmers (NABARD) / Starting new irrigation projects / Consolidation of land holding / Subsidies on fertilizers, free electricity/diesel to run the water pump / Introduction of green revolution / Setting up of agricultural universities. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: promoting high yielding variety seeds, agriculture price commission, easy loans/NABARD, new irrigation projects, consolidation of land holding, subsidies on fertilizers/free electricity, green revolution, agricultural universities
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two steps taken by the government to boost agricultural production are: (1) providing easy loans to farmers through institutions like NABARD, and (2) introducing the green revolution by promoting high-yielding variety seeds and modern farming techniques.
accepted_alternatives: Setting up of agriculture price commission
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the meaning of food crops, cash crops and plantation crops with examples and relate the chapter on agriculture with climate, water resources and soil.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name two varieties of millet grown in India.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Any two of: Jowar, Bajra, Ragi
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Jowar/ Bajra/ Ragi
key_points: Any two of: Jowar, Bajra, Ragi
marking_schemes.model_answer: Jowar and Bajra (any two from: Jowar, Bajra, Ragi).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Advise students to prepare a table/chart of climatic and soil requirements of each crop.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the soil requirement for growing millet?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Sandy alluvium/ black/ red (Any one)
key_points: Sandy alluvium or black or red soil (any one)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Sandy alluvium / black / red soil (any one).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Advise students to prepare a table/chart of climatic and soil requirements of each crop to make learning easier.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the picture of cotton crop given. Mention the climatic condition that is suitable for the cultivation of this crop.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Temperature: 18°C to 32°C. Rainfall: 50 cm to 80 cm / 200 frost free days / bright sunshine during harvest.
key_points: Temperature: 18°C to 32°C
Rainfall: 50 cm to 80 cm / 200 frost free days / bright sunshine during harvest
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cotton requires a temperature of 18°C to 32°C and a rainfall of 50 cm to 80 cm, with 200 frost-free days and bright sunshine during the harvest period.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the incorrect temperature range
Some candidates mentioned soil which was not asked for
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Advise students to prepare a table/chart of climatic and soil requirements of each crop. Explain the distribution of the crop by using a map.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the picture of cotton crop given. Name the state that produces the largest amount of this crop.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Maharashtra/Gujarat
key_points: Maharashtra or Gujarat
marking_schemes.model_answer: Maharashtra / Gujarat
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the distribution of the crop using a map.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the picture of cotton crop given. In which cropping season is this crop grown in India?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Kharif
key_points: Kharif
marking_schemes.model_answer: Kharif
common_errors: Many candidates wrote Summer / June to September instead of Kharif
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify the types of cropping seasons in India and give examples of crops grown in each cropping season.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Cultivation of wheat is confined to the northern part of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Ideal temperature of 10°C to 20°C that is suitable growth of wheat is available in north India / In north India winter rain occurs which is found suitable for its growth / 50 cm - 100 cm rain in north-west India. Wheat is a temperate crop. India is a warm country so cool climate is found in north during winter. (Any one)
key_points: Ideal temperature of 10°C to 20°C available in north India / cool climate in north during winter
Winter rain occurs in north India which suits wheat / wheat is a temperate crop
marking_schemes.model_answer: Wheat cultivation is confined to northern India because the ideal temperature of 10°C to 20°C required for wheat growth is available there during winter. Wheat is a temperate crop, and the cool winter climate with winter rains in north-western India provides suitable conditions.
accepted_alternatives: 50 cm–100 cm rainfall in north-west India
Wheat is a temperate crop needing cool climate
common_errors: Some candidates related wheat cultivation being confined to North India to alluvial soil instead of climate/temperature
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Relate the chapter on agriculture with chapters on climate, water resources and soil for better understanding.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Practicing mixed farming gives security to farmers.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: During drought and crop failures it provides income from livestock / extra income.
key_points: During drought and crop failures it provides income from livestock / extra income
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mixed farming gives security to farmers because during drought or crop failure, the livestock component of the farm provides an alternative source of income, ensuring that the farmer is not entirely dependent on a single crop.
common_errors: Some candidates gave the meaning of mixed farming instead of its advantages
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the highlights of different types of farming with the advantages of each.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Ratoon cropping is gaining popularity among sugarcane cultivators.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Mature faster / saves time and money / less labour required / cost effective. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: matures faster, saves time and money, less labour required, cost effective
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ratoon cropping is gaining popularity among sugarcane cultivators because the ratoon crop matures faster, saves time and money, requires less labour, and is cost effective as farmers do not need to replant the crop.
common_errors: Some candidates did not mention the crop (sugarcane) associated with ratoon cropping
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to mention the name of the crop for questions in which any term related to it is asked. Clearly explain terms such as ratooning, ginning, retting, etc.

marking_schemes.question_text: Where does the Bhilai Iron and Steel Plant get its supply of iron ore from?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Dalli-Rajhara Range / Singhbhum / Keonjhar / Durg / Bastar / Chandipur (any one)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Iron Ore – Dalli-Rajhara Range / Singhbhum/Keonjhar/ Durg/Bastar/ Chandipur. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: Dalli-Rajhara Range, Singhbhum, Keonjhar, Durg, Bastar, Chandipur
marking_schemes.model_answer: Dalli-Rajhara Range / Singhbhum / Keonjhar / Durg / Bastar / Chandipur (any one).
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the names of States instead of the specific mines
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Advise students to note whether mines/place or State has been asked, and then answer accordingly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Where does the Vishakhapatnam Steel Plant get its supply of iron ore from?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Iron Ore – Bailadila mines in Chhattisgarh/ Bastar.
key_points: Bailadila mines in Chhattisgarh / Bastar
marking_schemes.model_answer: Bailadila mines in Chhattisgarh / Bastar
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the names of States instead of the specific mines
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Advise students to note whether mines/place or State has been asked, and then answer accordingly.

marking_schemes.question_text: 'Karnataka has developed as an important state for the growth of the Silk industry.' Give two reasons to justify the statement.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Climate is suitable for sericulture / large market / skilled workers / latest technology available / favourable government policies / non-alkaline water or soft water present / licenced distributers present.
key_points: Any two of: climate suitable for sericulture, large market, skilled workers, latest technology available, favourable government policies, non-alkaline/soft water present, licensed distributors present
marking_schemes.model_answer: Karnataka has developed as an important silk-producing state because the climate is suitable for sericulture (mulberry cultivation and silkworm rearing), and the state has a large pool of skilled workers along with a large market, advanced technology, and favourable government policies.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the factors of location of industries given in the scope of syllabus.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to sugar industries: Why should these industries be located close to the sugarcane growing areas?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Sugarcane starts losing its sucrose after it is cut / to reduce the transportation cost / must be crushed within 48 hours / sugarcane is perishable.
key_points: Sugarcane starts losing its sucrose after being cut
Must be crushed within 48 hours / it is perishable
To reduce transportation cost
marking_schemes.model_answer: Sugar industries must be located close to sugarcane growing areas because sugarcane starts losing its sucrose content after it is cut and must be crushed within 48 hours. Being a perishable crop, transporting it over long distances would result in loss of sugar content and increased transportation costs.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the factors of location of industries given in the scope of syllabus.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to sugar industries: Name two by-products of the sugar industry.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Any two of: Molasses, Bagasse, Press mud
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Molasses / bagasse / press mud. (Any two)
key_points: Any two of: Molasses, Bagasse, Press mud
marking_schemes.model_answer: Molasses and Bagasse (any two from: Molasses, Bagasse, Press mud).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the classification of industries in detail.

marking_schemes.question_text: With reference to sugar industries: Mention one leading sugar producing state in North India and one in South India.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: North India: Uttar Pradesh / Bihar / Haryana / Punjab (any one); South India: Maharashtra / Karnataka / Tamil Nadu / Andhra Pradesh / Telangana (any one)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: North India – Uttar Pradesh / Bihar / Haryana / Punjab (Any one). South India – Maharashtra / Karnataka / Tamil Nadu / Andhra Pradesh / Telangana (Any one)
key_points: North India: any one of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana, Punjab
South India: any one of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana
marking_schemes.model_answer: North India: Uttar Pradesh. South India: Maharashtra (or any other accepted alternative for each).
common_errors: Some candidates wrote general names without stating whether the state is in North India or South India
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice to students to answer reasoning and application-based questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Ahmedabad is an important cotton textile producing centre in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Humid climate / availability of raw material / availability of skilled and unskilled labours / availability of cheap hydroelectricity / good transport network / port nearby / market / capital or credit facility available / soft water available / government support. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: humid climate, availability of raw material, skilled/unskilled labour, cheap hydroelectricity, good transport network, port nearby, market, capital/credit facility, soft water, government support
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ahmedabad is an important cotton textile centre because it has a humid climate suitable for spinning and weaving, ready availability of raw cotton from Gujarat, skilled and unskilled labour, good transport links, and access to capital and markets.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the factors of location of those industries that are given in scope of syllabus.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Cottage industries are significant for our economy.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Provides employment / Brings in foreign exchange / Need less built up area / Can be started with less capital investment / Uses local raw material / Keeps the traditions alive from one generation to another / Fulfil local need / low cost of transport. (Any one)
key_points: Any one of: provides employment, earns foreign exchange, needs less built-up area, less capital investment, uses local raw material, keeps traditions alive, fulfils local need, low transport cost
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cottage industries are significant for the economy because they provide employment to a large number of people, especially in rural areas, require very little capital investment and built-up area, use local raw materials, and help preserve traditional crafts from generation to generation.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the classification of industries in detail.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Petrochemical industries are usually located close to the oil refineries.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Raw materials used in petrochemical industries are mainly derived from petroleum hence these industries are located close to oil refineries.
key_points: Raw materials used in petrochemical industries are mainly derived from petroleum/oil refineries
marking_schemes.model_answer: Petrochemical industries are located close to oil refineries because their raw materials (such as naphtha, ethylene, propylene) are derived from petroleum and are produced at oil refineries, reducing transportation costs and ensuring a steady supply.
common_errors: Some candidates could not relate the question to the availability of raw material
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instruct students to read the question carefully before answering.

marking_schemes.question_text: 'Roadways are an important means of transport in India.' Give two reasons to justify the statement.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: They are cheap means of transport / They link villages to the urban areas / They can be constructed in the remote areas / difficult terrain / high altitudes / steep slope / They provide door-to-door service / They are safer means of transport for perishable items / Flexible usage. (Any two points)
key_points: Any two of: cheap means of transport, link villages to urban areas, can be constructed in remote/difficult terrain, door-to-door service, safer for perishable items, flexible usage
marking_schemes.model_answer: Roadways are an important means of transport in India because they are cheap and provide door-to-door service. They can be constructed even in remote areas and difficult terrain where other modes of transport are not feasible, and they link villages to urban areas.
accepted_alternatives: Can be constructed in remote/difficult terrain
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the importance of the means of transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why are South Indian rivers not ideal for the inland water transport?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: South Indian rivers are seasonal in nature / They have rapids and water falls and cataracts / They will have little water in hot season / Undulating terrain / Short river/swift river. (Any one point)
key_points: Any one of: seasonal in nature, have rapids/waterfalls/cataracts, little water in hot season, undulating terrain, short/swift rivers
marking_schemes.model_answer: South Indian rivers are not ideal for inland water transport because they are seasonal in nature with little water in the dry season, and they have numerous rapids, waterfalls and cataracts due to the undulating terrain, making them non-navigable.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the characteristics of rivers of North India and South India to enable students to understand why South Indian rivers are not ideal for inland water transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one advantage of coastal shipping.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Less maintenance cost / cheapest means of transport / ideal for export and import of bulky goods / causes less pollution / fuel efficient. (Any one point)
key_points: Any one of: less maintenance cost, cheapest means of transport, ideal for export and import of bulky goods, causes less pollution, fuel efficient
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of coastal shipping is that it is the cheapest means of transport, ideal for carrying bulky goods for export and import, and is also fuel efficient and causes less pollution.
accepted_alternatives: Ideal for export and import of bulky goods
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss coastal shipping in detail.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Nearly seventy percent of Indians do not use air transport.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Air transport is very expensive hence it is not used by many people / carry less luggage / not comfortable for long journey / no airport in small town.
key_points: Air transport is very expensive / no airports in small towns / carry less luggage
marking_schemes.model_answer: Nearly seventy percent of Indians do not use air transport primarily because it is very expensive and unaffordable for most of the population. Additionally, airports are not available in small towns, and air travel allows only limited luggage.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the advantages and disadvantages of all means of transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: A well-developed transport network is important for industrial growth.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Transportation helps in easy movement of raw materials and finished goods / connect backward areas / mobility of skilled and unskilled labour / decentralised growth.
key_points: Transportation helps in easy movement of raw materials and finished goods
Connects backward areas / mobility of skilled and unskilled labour / decentralised growth
marking_schemes.model_answer: A well-developed transport network is important for industrial growth because it facilitates the easy movement of raw materials to factories and finished goods to markets. It also enables the mobility of skilled and unskilled labour and helps connect backward areas to centres of industrial activity.
accepted_alternatives: Mobility of skilled and unskilled labour
common_errors: Many candidates were unable to relate transport to industries and wrote vague answers
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Relate a well-developed transport network to growth of industries and the economy as a whole.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Water transport is not as popular as land transport in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Water transport is limited to areas which have navigable water source. It is slow and not well connected.
key_points: Water transport is limited to areas with navigable water sources
It is slow and not well connected
marking_schemes.model_answer: Water transport is not as popular as land transport in India because it is limited to areas that have navigable rivers or coastlines. It is also slow and not well connected to the hinterland, making it inconvenient for most passengers and cargo.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the advantages and disadvantages of all means of transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: 'The railway is an important means of transport as compared to airways.' State two reasons to support the statement.
