marking_schemes.scheme_text: It carries bulky raw materials and heavy goods / It is cheaper than airways / Caters to more number of passengers at one time / Can carry more amount of goods / Comfortable for long journey. (Any two points)
key_points: Any two of: carries bulky raw materials and heavy goods, cheaper than airways, caters to more passengers at one time, can carry more goods, comfortable for long journey
marking_schemes.model_answer: Railways are more important than airways because they are far cheaper than air travel and can carry a larger number of passengers and heavier/bulkier goods at one time. Railways are also more comfortable for long journeys.
accepted_alternatives: Carries bulky raw materials and heavy goods
Caters to more passengers at one time
Can carry more amount of goods
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the advantages and disadvantages of all means of transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one disadvantage of rail transport.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The flow of goods and passengers are hampered in India as the railways' operation is on three gauges / Shifting from one gauge to another is time consuming and expensive / Perishable items cannot stand the delay / The tracks are not able to carry increased goods and accidents are becoming frequent / Poor maintenance of tracks / Outdated engines and compartments / It causes pollution / Overcrowded / Delays. (Any one point)
key_points: Any one of: three gauges hampering movement, shifting gauges is time-consuming/expensive, perishable items cannot withstand delays, tracks unable to carry increased load/frequent accidents, poor maintenance, outdated engines/compartments, causes pollution, overcrowded, delays
marking_schemes.model_answer: One disadvantage of rail transport is that India's railway network operates on three different gauges, which hampers the smooth flow of goods and passengers as shifting from one gauge to another is time-consuming and expensive.
accepted_alternatives: Tracks unable to carry increased goods/frequent accidents
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the advantages and disadvantages of all means of transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: What impact does the waste accumulation have on the quality of air around us?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Waste accumulation results in air pollution which may cause acid rain and several air-borne diseases / bad odour / release harmful greenhouse gases / chemicals near the underground water by leakage.
key_points: Waste accumulation results in air pollution
May cause acid rain, airborne diseases, bad odour, release of harmful greenhouse gases
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waste accumulation results in air pollution by releasing harmful greenhouse gases and causing bad odour. This can lead to acid rain and several airborne diseases affecting the health of people living nearby.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain clearly to the students the impact of waste accumulation on the quality of air/water.

marking_schemes.question_text: What impact does the waste accumulation have on the quality of water around us?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Water pollution affects human health and also animal life on land it also affects aquatic animals adversely / eutrophication / biomagnification.
key_points: Waste accumulation causes water pollution
Affects human health, animal life, aquatic animals / eutrophication / biomagnification
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waste accumulation leads to water pollution which adversely affects human health and aquatic life. It can cause eutrophication and biomagnification, and leaching of chemicals can contaminate underground water sources.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain clearly to the students the impact of waste accumulation on the quality of air/water.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two ways in which the decomposition of waste in open areas can affect human health.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It may lead to foul smell and several diseases such as malaria, cholera etc., may be caused due to flies and other insects that carry the disease causing bacteria which grow in the decomposing waste / it produces harmful gases which pollute the air around us / rainwater may carry the pathogens from the waste to our water bodies and so pollute the water which affects human health / biomagnification. (Two points)
key_points: Any two of: foul smell / diseases like malaria and cholera caused by flies/insects breeding in waste, harmful gases produced polluting the air, rainwater carrying pathogens to water bodies polluting them, biomagnification
marking_schemes.model_answer: Decomposition of waste in open areas affects human health in two ways: (1) flies and insects breeding in decomposing waste carry disease-causing bacteria, spreading diseases like malaria and cholera, and (2) harmful gases produced during decomposition pollute the surrounding air, causing respiratory problems.
accepted_alternatives: Rainwater carrying pathogens to water bodies
common_errors: Some candidates wrote general points
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain clearly the effect of decomposition of waste in open areas on human health.

marking_schemes.question_text: What can an individual do to reduce waste at home?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Individual may use carry bags / adopt reusable containers and utensils / use rechargeable batteries / use computer storage system rather than paper / recycle used paper / compost solid kitchen waste / reduce usage / reuse by following 3R. (One point)
key_points: Any one of: use carry bags, reusable containers/utensils, rechargeable batteries, computer storage instead of paper, recycle used paper, compost kitchen waste, follow 3R (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle)
marking_schemes.model_answer: An individual can reduce waste at home by following the 3R principle — reducing usage, reusing containers and utensils, and recycling used paper. Composting solid kitchen waste and using rechargeable batteries are also effective measures.
accepted_alternatives: Use computer storage instead of paper
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the disadvantages of using synthetic products relating it to present environmental issues faced by our country.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why must segregation of waste be done before disposal?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It will help in safe disposal and will cause lesser pollution.
key_points: Segregation helps in safe disposal and causes lesser pollution
marking_schemes.model_answer: Segregation of waste must be done before disposal because it helps ensure safe and efficient disposal of different types of waste (biodegradable and non-biodegradable), and thereby causes lesser pollution.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the meaning of segregation instead of the reason for segregating waste before disposal
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain clearly to students the different methods of waste disposal and their advantages with examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: How has composting proven to be a great help in managing waste?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It not only reduces waste accumulation but also increases plant growth.
key_points: Composting reduces waste accumulation
Also increases plant growth (acts as manure/fertilizer)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Composting has proven to be a great help in managing waste because it not only reduces waste accumulation by converting organic waste into useful material, but also increases plant growth by serving as a rich natural fertilizer/manure.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Regularly revise the topics with students.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Trees must be planted in the industrial areas.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Trees give out oxygen and take in carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide emitted by industries / trees control noise pollution / air pollution / maintain temperature.
key_points: Trees absorb carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide emitted by industries and give out oxygen
Trees control noise pollution / air pollution / maintain temperature
marking_schemes.model_answer: Trees must be planted in industrial areas because they absorb harmful gases such as carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide emitted by industries while releasing oxygen. They also help control noise pollution, maintain temperature, and reduce air pollution.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to write the answers to the point and instruct them to use correct terms.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Chemical fertilizers must be replaced by organic manure.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The chemicals in chemical fertilizers combine with plant nutrients and the plants are consumed by animals and humans which is harmful (benefits of organic manure or harmful effects of chemical fertilisers may be written).
key_points: Chemical fertilizers are harmful as chemicals combine with plant nutrients and enter the food chain through plants consumed by animals and humans
Organic manure benefits may also be stated
marking_schemes.model_answer: Chemical fertilizers must be replaced by organic manure because the chemicals in fertilizers combine with plant nutrients and are taken up by plants. When these plants are consumed by animals and humans, the chemicals enter the food chain causing health hazards. Organic manure is safe, eco-friendly and improves soil health.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the disadvantages of using synthetic products relating it to present environmental issues.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Plastic and polythene products must be banned.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Plastic and polythene products must be banned because they are non-biodegradable and take hundreds of years to decompose. If these plastics are ingested by animals like cattle or marine life like whales, it can lead to their death. They cause clogging of drains / pollute soil / obstruct the seepage of water.
key_points: Plastic and polythene are non-biodegradable and take hundreds of years to decompose
If ingested by animals/marine life can lead to their death / clog drains / pollute soil / obstruct water seepage
marking_schemes.model_answer: Plastic and polythene products must be banned because they are non-biodegradable and take hundreds of years to decompose. They clog drains, pollute soil, obstruct water seepage, and if ingested by animals like cattle or marine life like whales, can lead to their death.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote vague answers such as 'it is bad for environment and humans'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the disadvantages of using synthetic products relating it to present environmental issues faced by our country.
